title: Park Geun-hye: Presidential Government, Sewol, Corruption, Candlelight Mobilization, and Impeachment
description: An editorial introduction to Park Geun-hye: Presidential Government, Sewol, Corruption, Candlelight Mobilization, and Impeachment, part of the expanding KOREA history archive.

blocks.title: Democracy faced a crisis of trust
paragraphs: The presidency of Park Geun-hye became a focal point for public debate over accountability, political influence, and the responsibilities of elected leadership. The Sewol ferry disaster generated profound grief and scrutiny of public institutions, while later revelations of corruption intensified political protest. These were distinct events with different immediate causes, but both contributed to questions about state competence and the relationship between office and public trust.

blocks.title: Candlelight gatherings as political practice
paragraphs: Large, repeated demonstrations showed how public assemblies could function within a constitutional political order. Participants expressed a range of concerns, and the movement's peaceful character became part of its public significance. Constitutional institutions ultimately played a decisive role in the impeachment process. The relationship between street mobilization and legal procedure is central: neither alone explains the full transition.

blocks.title: Institutional consequences
paragraphs: The episode illustrates both the vulnerability and resilience of democratic systems. Elections, courts, legislatures, news organizations, and civic groups interact in periods of crisis, sometimes reinforcing and sometimes challenging one another. A historical account should avoid reducing a complex movement to a single party's narrative and instead follow the sequence of evidence, protest, institutional decisions, and political change.
